title: AI Voiceover for Video: How to Narrate a Short Film
summary: Add an AI voiceover to your video in 4 steps: write the lines, voice them, pick takes and leave silence. With the real narration of the short To My Grandma.
body_markdown:
### What is an AI voiceover?


An AI voiceover is narration spoken by a generated voice, made from written text instead of a recording session. It is laid over video as a narrator's voice, unlike dialogue, which a character speaks on screen.


### How do I add an AI voiceover to a video?


Write the narration as short lines, generate each line with a text to speech model, then place the audio clips under the shots in a video editor. In Flick, Text to Voice makes the lines and the Video Editor's Music track holds them under the picture.


### Is there a free AI voiceover for video?


Yes. Text to Voice in Flick, with Eleven v3 or Eleven v4, is on the Free plan at 8 credits a generation, and a new account gets 100 credits when it signs up.


### Can I make an AI voiceover in my own voice?


Yes. In Flick, Text to Voice with Seed Audio 1.0 takes up to three voice clips you attach as references and speaks new lines in that voice. You can also import your own recording as audio and place it on the timeline. Use only voices you have the right to use.


### How long should narration be in a short film?


As short as the story allows: narration works best as a few lines with silence between them, not a continuous track. To My Grandma, a short made in Flick, tells its story in 6 narrated lines over a film of 1:38.


### Can an AI voiceover sound emotional?


Yes. Write the line the way it should be spoken, with punctuation where the voice should pause, and add cues in square brackets such as \[whispers\] or \[laughs\] in Text to Voice. Generate a few takes and keep the one whose feeling fits the shot.


### Can AI voiceover speak other languages?


Yes. Eleven v4 speaks more than 90 languages, and the voice picker in Text to Voice filters voices by language. Not every voice supports every language, so preview the voice first.
